email.from: Owner's vessel technical management (Fern Estuary Shipping, fictional) <technical@fernestuary-shipping.example>
email.subject: MV FERN ESTUARY - Red Sea passage declined (war risks)
email.body:
Dear Operations,

MV FERN ESTUARY, Fujairah to Antwerp

Owners have reviewed the security advisory issued overnight for the southern Red Sea. The Master and owners consider the passage through Bab el-Mandeb exposes the vessel to war risks, and owners will not proceed that way, under the charter party's war risks clause.

Please give alternative orders, for which we propose the Cape of Good Hope. The Master is keeping well clear of the area meanwhile.

Best regards,
Marine department
Owner's vessel technical management (Fern Estuary Shipping, fictional)

result.result:
The owner has the right to decline the passage through the Red Sea under the war risks clause of the charter party, and the resulting extra time and bunkers are for the charterers' (your company's) account. The route via the Cape of Good Hope adds 4,898.1 nm and approximately 16.3 days, with a new ETA of 25 Feb 18:00 UTC. Current VLSFO on board is insufficient to cover this route with the required 3-day reserve, leaving a shortfall of about 25.8 t; bunkers must therefore be arranged on the way.

The operator should decide whether to confirm this new route. If agreed, the following steps will be taken: (a) a reply to the owner confirming the route, (b) an ETA notice to the agent and receiver (as indicated by the notice check) with the new ETA, and (c) a voyage management system entry for the Antwerp port call ETA. I recommend that nothing be sent until the operator answers.
